_meta.title: mPulse Query API Reference Catalog
_meta.purpose: Reference names and API behavior to reduce repeated discovery and avoidable query errors.
_meta.generated_by: Empirically verified vs live mpulse MCP (app=app-a) + Akamai TechDocs endpoint reference pages + Akamai cli-mpulse; bandwith-block spelling and custom-dimension usage confirmed by app owner.
_meta.custom_metric_source: App-specific CUSTOM metrics/timers are not in these enums. Get them from Repository/Objects API domain['custom_metrics'] (github.com/akamai/mPulseAPI.jl) or the dashboard report-builder.

maintenance.mode: Manually maintained static reference; no automatic synchronization with the upstream API.
maintenance.sources: Akamai TechDocs, cli-mpulse choices, and recorded live API checks. Keep source/verification dates when updating entries.
maintenance.review_scope: Descriptions reconciled with the local implementation; this is not a new live verification of all API claims.
maintenance.update_process: Review API changes, verify affected behavior, edit this JSON and regression tests (and Python code when behavior changes), deploy, then restart the MCP server.
maintenance.runtime: Query metadata is loaded and cached per process. The packaged catalog is required; missing or invalid metadata raises a clear configuration error during import/startup. Deploy edits and restart the server. describe_query selects reference content; textual constraints are not all executable validation rules.
maintenance.metadata_source: endpoint_params is the canonical query metadata registry; query_types.py loads typed Python views without a second hard-coded API table.

CRITICAL_same_metric_different_name_per_.note: A physical metric is named ONE way for timers-metrics (CamelCase) and a DIFFERENT way for metrics-by-dimension (snake_case). Do NOT convert mechanically: only ~23% of names survive a CamelCase->snake_case rewrite (verified 2026-11-02 against both enums). Traps: Img->image_, Bcn->beacon_, Total*->asset_*, Avg* prefix dropped, *CompressionRatio->*_compression_rate. Pick the name from the endpoint's own valid_metrics enum.
CRITICAL_same_metric_different_name_per_.note_TotalRequestCount: TotalRequestCount is NOT in the timers-metrics docs enum (its Total* group lists 8 items, matching the doc's '97' count) yet it RETURNS a valid series in the live API (verified: returns a valid series). Treat as working-but-undocumented. Per-content-type counts (PageRequestCount, JsRequestCount, ImgRequestCount, ...) ARE documented.

query_types.note: Canonical query types and their metadata are defined once under endpoint_params; underscore-prefixed entries there are reference notes.
query_types.usage_constraints: The date parameter selects one calendar day; Between selects a range with an exclusive end. Time-series resolution depends on the endpoint and period. Results depend on timezone; empty filtered results require interpretation.

metrics_for_timers_metrics__metric_param.endpoint: timers-metrics (also summary/histogram/by-minute use the `timer` param family, not this)
metrics_for_timers_metrics__metric_param.multiple: The API accepts repeated metric= and timer= keys in the same query. get_metrics accepts a string or JSON list for metric and timer; query accepts JSON lists in params. The client expands lists to repeated query keys. get_aggregate groups requested metrics and timers into one timers-metrics query per unique period/percentile.
metrics_for_timers_metrics__metric_param.prefixes: Bcn(beacon), Css, Font, Html, Img(image), Js, Other, Page, Total(all), Xhr. Suffixes: RequestCount, TransferSize, DecodedBodySize, CompressionRatio, ByteCompressionRatio, BrowserCacheHitRatio, CdnCacheHitRatio, CdnEdgeTime, OriginTime.
metrics_for_timers_metrics__metric_param.param_name: metric (singular, repeated for multiple values), e.g. metric=Beacons&metric=TotalRequestCount; timer=PageLoad&timer=LargestContentfulPaint can be included in the same query.

metrics_for_metrics_by_dimension__metric.multiple: Comma-separated list in ONE `metrics` param, e.g. metrics=beacons,largest_contentful_paint (verified live).
constraints: apperror_message/code/source/type dimensions ignore requested metrics and always return AppErrors, AppErrorsPct, ErrorsPerPage (verified_live 2026-10-29).
page_group, full_url, network_error_code dimensions do NOT support session, session_length, session_duration, bounce_rate (page_group + session_duration -> HTTP 400, verified_live 2026-10-29).
network_error_code does NOT support errors_per_page (HTTP 400, verified_live 2026-10-29). beacon_type DOES support it, contrary to the docs (verified_live 2026-10-29).
metrics_for_metrics_by_dimension__metric.metric_singular_ignored: At the upstream API, singular metric is ignored and app-default columns may be returned. The MCP query tool rejects singular metric before HTTP; get_breakdown exposes the correct plural metrics argument.

extra_params.limit: int 1-100; mPulse default is 10 rows; the MCP query tool sends 100 unless told otherwise; results come pre-sorted

timers_for_timer_param.endpoints: timers-metrics, summary, histogram, by-minute (and timer-by-* reports)
timers_for_timer_param.note: Unrecognized `timer` SILENTLY falls back to PageLoad (no error) - always check response series id == requested name. For custom timers use custom-timer=<name>, or timer=CustomTimer[0-9] by index. Invalid custom-timer DOES 400.
timers_for_timer_param.param_name: timer (singular; repeat the key for multiple)

drilldown_filter_params.note: Hyphenated. Used to FILTER any report. NOTE the API misspells bandwidth as 'bandwith-block' (missing d, verified live). Custom dimensions filter via custom-dimension-<label>=<value>, e.g. custom-dimension-branch=uk to filter to branch=uk. <label> = the custom dimension name, lowercased with spaces replaced by underscores.

metrics_by_dimension__dimension_split_en.note: Underscored built-in names for the metrics-by-dimension split. The catalog contains verified names and may not cover future system dimensions. Custom dimensions also use dimension=<label>; app-specific custom labels are declared in mpulse_apps.json. A name missing from both lists is unclassified, not necessarily custom.

verification.method: Read-only Query API checks confirmed the five 2024 system dimensions on this endpoint.

dimension_values__dimension_enum.note: underscored. Valid `dimension` values for the dimension-values query. connection_type is NOT here -> that's why dimension-values with connection-type 400s. (The MCP accepts hyphenated aliases like beacon-type/device-type and maps them.) CUSTOM DIMENSIONS ARE NOT ALLOWED here (built-in only); use metrics-by-dimension to break down by a custom dimension.

verification.method: Read-only Query API checks confirmed the five 2024 system dimensions on this endpoint.

beacon-type.note: 'page view' has a space. Live data for app-a currently shows only 'page view' and 'xhr'.

dimension_over_time__dimension_enum.note: underscored. Valid `dimension` for dimension-over-time (built-in only; custom NOT allowed).

verification.method: Read-only Query API checks confirmed the five 2024 system dimensions on this endpoint.

percentile.note: one value per query; p50 & p75 need two calls

timezone.note: Java-parseable names e.g. US/Eastern, Europe/London, Asia/Shanghai

date.note: The API date parameter selects one calendar day. Without date/date-comparator the API defaults to Today; get_summary/get_histogram/get_timers/get_metrics require an explicit date or date_comparator. get_breakdown/query may use the API default.

date_comparator.note: Between needs date-start & date-end (date-end exclusive); Last needs trailing-seconds. ThisWeek = 00:00 seven days ago until now; ThisMonth = 00:00 on the same day last month until now (verified_live 2026-10-29). Neither is a calendar week or month. No date at all = Today. Unsupported values return HTTP 500 and are rejected by the server up front (verified_live 2026-10-29).

date_start_end.note: For Between. Docs: date-end must be GREATER than date-start. Live behavior: date-end is EXCLUSIVE (June = start 2026-06-01, end 2026-07-01). Multi-day ranges auto-coarsen buckets (~2d hourly, ~30d daily).

items.text: Invalid `timer` or `metric` name -> silent fallback to PageLoad (no error). Validate response series id == requested name.

timers-metrics: pass a JSON LIST for multiple `metric`/`timer` values; the client expands it to repeated keys (verified_live 2026-10-29). The default PageLoad timer series comes back alongside requested metrics.

timers-metrics `latest` = aggregate over the WHOLE selected period (e.g. Beacons daily latest == total n; percentile metric latest == period-wide percentile). history[] is the per-bucket series. For a monthly p75/p50 read `latest`, do not average daily history.
date-end is EXCLUSIVE for Between despite docs saying 'greater than'.
dimension naming differs by context: FILTER params are hyphenated (beacon-type); the split `dimension` value is underscored (beacon_type).
Param misspelling is REAL (verified live): the bandwidth filter param is `bandwith-block` (missing 'd'); `bandwidth-block` does not work.

Custom dimensions: filter with custom-dimension-<label>=<value> on endpoints supporting filters; split with metrics-by-dimension dimension=<custom_name>. Declare labels in mpulse_apps.json and inspect list_custom_dimensions. The MCP server does not discover custom labels automatically.
metrics-by-dimension: use metrics (PLURAL, comma-separated). Upstream ignores singular metric; the MCP query tool rejects it before HTTP. get_breakdown exposes a metrics list and joins it correctly.
metrics-by-dimension computes percentiles (timer p75 by dimension matches timers-metrics). Mixing count metrics (beacons) with percentile metrics in one call works (verified_live 2026-10-29).

Multiple metric/timer values are repeat-key only on timers-metrics; supported filters and custom-dimension-* filters also use repeated keys. Pass JSON lists through query, get_metrics, or the supported dedicated filter arguments. get_breakdown joins its metrics list into the plural comma-separated metrics parameter. Single-value timer/metric endpoints do not accept lists.
metric-per-page-load-time uses a single `metric` with a distinct enum (BounceRate + CustomMetric0-9).

metrics-by-dimension, app-error-summary and dimension-over-time return only mPulse's default top 10 rows without a native `limit`. The MCP query tool sends its top-level `limit` (default 100, or 10 for dimension-over-time) and sets truncated.by == 'server' when the result fills it. Contrary to the docs, `limit` works for country/page_group/browser (verified live).
Unsupported date-comparator values (Yesterday, Last7Days, Last6Hours, …) return HTTP 500, not 400. Use date=YYYY-MM-DD for yesterday and Between for a range.

Chart-style endpoints (by-minute, histogram, bandwidth, sessions-per-page-load-time, dimension-over-time) default to series-format=js, a JavaScript-literal string. The server forces series-format=json.

dimension-over-time: without an explicit interval, the API selects resolution based on the period. Use interval when resolution matters; history_mode reduces returned points after the API response is received.
metrics-by-dimension with an apperror_* dimension ignores the requested metrics and always returns AppErrors, AppErrorsPct and ErrorsPerPage.

ThisWeek and ThisMonth are trailing windows, not calendar periods: ThisWeek starts at 00:00 seven days ago and ThisMonth at 00:00 on the same day last month, both ending now, in the request timezone (verified live). For a calendar month use Between with date_start=YYYY-MM-01 and date_end=the first day of the next month. Results include period.resolved with the exact range.

metrics-by-dimension `metrics` values ARE validated by mPulse: an invalid name returns HTTP 400 'Invalid metric' (verified live 2026-11-02) — no silent fallback, unlike timer/metric on the timers-metrics family. Matching is case/underscore-insensitive (Image_Transfer_Size works).

behavioral_gotchas._note: applies_to lists the query-types a gotcha concerns ('all' = every query-type); describe_query shows only the matching ones unless verbose=True.

api_rate_limits.confidence: Reference values; upstream quotas have not been reverified in this implementation review.
api_rate_limits.runtime_note: client.py currently applies concurrency=3 and per-minute=100 locally per client process. Hour/day values here are advisory; they do not configure the limiter and are not separately enforced.

drilldown_combination_rule.rule: Unsupported dimension combos return EMPTY data, not an error -> empty may mean 'combo unsupported', not 'no traffic'.

worked_example.goal: app-a monthly p75 asset requests/page, page-view beacons, June 2026
worked_example.read: response series where id=='TotalRequestCount' -> latest (the period p75 value)

custom_dimensions.split_usage: metrics-by-dimension dimension=<custom_name>  e.g. dimension=branch (metric broken down by 'branch')
custom_dimensions.label_rule: <label> is the custom dimension name lowercased, spaces -> underscores. Use .NONE to match beacons with no value.
custom_dimensions.enumeration: Custom labels are declared per app in mpulse_apps.json and exposed through list_custom_dimensions and describe_query(app=...). This implementation does not discover them automatically from mPulse. Built-in dimension enums do not include custom labels; an undeclared custom label may pass through with an advisory.

custom_dimension_support.confidence: user_provided (app owner) + verified_live 2026-10-29: dimension-values/dimension-over-time with a custom name -> HTTP 400
custom_dimension_support.note: Among dimension split endpoints, custom labels are accepted by metrics-by-dimension only; dimension-values and dimension-over-time accept built-in split dimensions. Custom-dimension filters are a separate capability on endpoints supporting drilldowns. Dedicated tools expose custom_dimension_filters with scalar or list values.

metrics_for_metric_per_page_load_time__m.note: Completely different metric name space from the other endpoints; only one metric per call.

parameter_mechanics.how_to_pass: For timers-metrics, get_metrics accepts a string or JSON list for metric and timer; query accepts lists under params. Supported dedicated filters and custom_dimension_filters also accept strings or lists. The client expands lists to repeated query keys. get_breakdown accepts a metrics list and joins it with commas; generic query uses a comma-joined metrics string (a string list is also joined by its preparer). Single-value endpoint parameters take scalars.
parameter_mechanics.comma_also_accepted_for_filters: country=KR,JP returns the same as repeated country keys (verified_live 2026-10-29); other filters untested.

endpoint_params._note: Per-endpoint special params beyond the shared date/timezone/drilldown-filter set. 'filters' = the standard drilldown filter params apply (repeat-key).

summary.summary: Aggregate stats for a timer: median, margin of error, count, p95/p98.

special_params.series-format: js|json, default js (a JS-literal string); the server always sends json

histogram.summary: Distribution (buckets) for a timer over the period.
histogram.response_shape: {chartTitle, datasetName, series:{series:[{name, aPoints:[{s,e,c}], buckets, median, p95, p98, kValue}]}}

special_params.series-format: js|json, default js (a JS-literal string); the server always sends json

by-minute.summary: A single timer's value by minute over time (time series).
by-minute.notes: Use for one timer. For multiple timers/metrics use 'timers-metrics'.

timers-metrics.notes: metric defaults to 'Beacons', timer to 'PageLoad'. Multiple metrics/timers via REPEATED keys (pass a JSON list).
timers-metrics.summary: Values for multiple timers or metrics by minute over time.
timers-metrics.aggregation: period aggregate in latest; history is a time series

dimension-values.notes: Drilldown filters are ignored, and custom or unknown dimensions return HTTP 400 (verified_live 2026-10-29).
dimension-values.summary: All observed values for a given dimension.
dimension-values.aggregation: distinct values observed over the period

special_params.limit: 1-10, default 10. mPulse rejects >10 upstream (recorded live 2026-10-29), but the MCP query tool lowers over-max requested values to 10 with a correction note before HTTP. Values below 1 or values that cannot be converted to an integer are rejected.
special_params.series-format: js|json, default js (a JS-literal string); the server always sends json

dimension-over-time.notes: Without `interval`, mPulse selects an interval based on the period; set an explicit interval when resolution matters. Custom dimensions and dimension-values-only names (e.g. bw_block) return HTTP 400; use bandwidth_block, browser_version etc. (verified_live 2026-10-29). Response: {labelNames, data:{series:[{name, aPoints}]}}.
dimension-over-time.aggregation: per-interval time series per dimension value

special_params.limit: 1-100. mPulse returns only the top 10 rows when limit is omitted, so the MCP query tool always sends one (its top-level `limit`, default 100). The docs say limit is not valid for page_group/browser/country/bw_block/ab_test, but live (2026-10-29) it IS honored for page_group, browser and country; bw_block and ab_test are unverified.

constraints: apperror_message/code/source/type dimensions ignore requested metrics and always return AppErrors, AppErrorsPct, ErrorsPerPage (verified_live 2026-10-29).
page_group, full_url, network_error_code dimensions do NOT support session, session_length, session_duration, bounce_rate (page_group + session_duration -> HTTP 400, verified_live 2026-10-29).
network_error_code does NOT support errors_per_page (HTTP 400, verified_live 2026-10-29). beacon_type DOES support it, contrary to the docs (verified_live 2026-10-29).
metrics-by-dimension.summary: Metric values broken down by a dimension.

value_params.metric: single, default BounceRate (own enum: BounceRate + CustomMetric0-9)

metric-per-page-load-time.notes: Default metric is BounceRate; other names (e.g. Beacons) return HTTP 400 (verified_live 2026-10-29).
metric-per-page-load-time.summary: A metric segmented by page-load-time ranges.

special_params.series-format: js|json, default js (a JS-literal string); the server always sends json

sessions-per-page-load-time.notes: No metric, no percentile, no limit.
sessions-per-page-load-time.summary: Session counts segmented by page-load-time ranges.

special_params.limit: 1-100, mPulse default 10 (verified_live 2026-10-29). The MCP query tool sends its top-level `limit` (default 100).

app-error-summary.summary: Aggregated application errors (messages, codes, sources, types).

page-groups.notes: Native `limit` is ignored (verified_live 2026-10-29); use the MCP client-side `limit` (default cap 100). `percentile` is honored (verified_live 2026-10-29).

browsers.notes: Native `limit` is ignored (verified_live 2026-10-29); use the MCP client-side `limit` (default cap 100). Returns ~1,800 rows for a day.

ab-tests.notes: Native `limit` is ignored (verified_live 2026-10-29); use the MCP client-side `limit` (default cap 100).

special_params.series-format: js|json, default js (a JS-literal string); the server always sends json

geography.notes: Native `limit` is ignored (verified_live 2026-10-29); use the MCP client-side `limit` (default cap 100).
